cases.scenario: A 90-day churn model deployed three weeks ago. A stakeholder asks whether it is performing as expected.
pass_if: States that realised performance cannot be measured until the label horizon elapses, and names the date it will be available
Reports what is available now: feature drift, prediction drift, reference-cohort stability, pipeline health
Distinguishes leading indicators from the lagging confirmation
Offers a short-horizon proxy if one exists, labelled as a proxy with its historical correlation
Does not report an unavailable realised lift as if it were measured
fail_if: Reports a realised lift figure computed on unresolved labels
Says nothing can be known yet
Presents drift stability as proof of model performance

cases.scenario: Score distribution PSI jumped to 0.31 this week. Feature PSI is unchanged and the outcome rate is stable.
pass_if: Identifies the scoring pipeline as the most likely cause, not the market
Prescribes the reference cohort as the first check, because it settles the question in one query
Explains the three-channel diagnostic rather than reporting a generic model-health alert
Does not recommend retraining as the first action
fail_if: Attributes the shift to market conditions
Reports the PSI number with no diagnosis

cases.scenario: A model is submitted for acceptance with PR-AUC 0.19 and no baseline measured.
pass_if: States that acceptance cannot be granted without a baseline and names why
Reports the model's metrics, which are computable, and contextualises PR-AUC against the base rate
Names exactly what is needed: the existing rule scored on the same holdout, and the majority-class floor
Does not accept or reject on the model's own numbers alone
fail_if: Accepts the model on PR-AUC alone
Rejects the model without identifying the missing input
Reconstructs a baseline from memory and treats it as measured

cases.scenario: A feature-drift alert has fired every week for two months. The team stopped reading it.
pass_if: Identifies the alert as mistuned against its expected frequency
States that an alert people ignore is worse than none, because it provides false assurance
Prescribes re-thresholding or retirement rather than adding another alert
Requires every alert to carry an owner, an executable action and an expected frequency
fail_if: Recommends more alerts or a dashboard
Treats sixty consecutive firings as sixty findings
Leaves the alert in place unchanged

cases.scenario: Aggregate lift 3.4x. On enterprise the model gets 1.2x against the existing rule's 1.6x, on 44 positives.
pass_if: Accepts with a scope limit rather than accepting or rejecting outright
Reports the enterprise figures with the positive count and the interval width
Records the segment as out-of-scope in the model card with the reason
States that a split deployment is a better outcome than one score everywhere
Does not present the wide-interval enterprise result as a precise measurement
fail_if: Accepts for all segments on the aggregate number
Omits the segment breakdown from the verdict

cases.scenario: A monthly automatic retraining job promotes the new model without comparing it to the incumbent.
pass_if: States that retraining must be gated, with the new model evaluated against both the incumbent and the original baseline on a fresh holdout
Explains the failure mode: each retrain inherits the last one's drift and nobody compares, so the model gets worse silently
Requires the previous version to remain runnable and the rollback to be tested
Notes that a label-version or feature-version change is a new model, not a retrain
Routes promotion through write-gate
